member.name: T:TRNRun.Internal.DaemonProcess
member.summary: A running trnrund, read by a background thread.
member.remarks: The thread sorts each stdout line: replies go to the waiting request, matched by id, and changed notifications wake and . trnrund's stdout ends only after its final changes are saved, so the end of stdout is how a crashed daemon is noticed. The thread then records the exit before waking waiters, so they never wait for it themselves. stderr is captured rather than shown: trnrund writes to it only before a fatal exit, and that text is added to the reporting the exit. Requests are serialized, so any thread may send one. Every await resumes on the thread pool, so the synchronous members, which wait on the asynchronous ones, never deadlock on a caller's synchronization context.

member.name: T:TRNRun.SimulationSettings
member.summary: TRNRun options for a simulation, with named, typed properties.

remarks.para: Each property maps to a trnrun.exe command-line flag, noted in its documentation, passed as --name:value. A property left is not passed, so TRNRun's own default applies; run trnrun.exe --help for them. new SimulationSettings() therefore passes nothing. The trnrun.exe executable itself is chosen per daemon, with , since one daemon runs every simulation with the same runner. Relative paths are interpreted from the current working directory.
trnrund checks the values with TRNRun's own parser when a run is added. checks that a set exists, so a missing installation fails before runs are queued.

member.summary: Shared launch-detection timeout in milliseconds (--detectTimeout); 0 means unlimited. If is enabled and TRNSYS is still running, expiration yields TIMEOUT; otherwise detection proceeds into monitoring. Detection holds the session-wide launch mutex.
